description:
🔴 **THE MERGE GATE IS A NO-OP.** `.chief/verify.sh` is the untouched scaffold: it prints *"verify: no checks configured yet — edit .chief/verify.sh (allowing merge)"* and `exit 0`. Measured 2026-08-13 — koine and cuneiform were the only two repos in the tree still on the stub, and cuneiform's was fixed by its `196`. So **every koine tasklist merges unverified**, and koine currently has 13 live tasklists with 10 ready to run.

**This is cheap here, because the checks already exist and are not wired.** `scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs` already gates every relative Markdown link and `#heading` anchor — the two ways this repo's prose goes silently stale — and `scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` gates the tasklist vocabulary. Neither runs at merge. Beyond those, koine holds three classes of machine-checkable asset that nothing verifies: `schemas/*.schema.json` (JSON Schema validity, and that every `$ref` resolves), `registry/*.tsv` (the shared relation and entity-type registries — column shape, no duplicate ids, referential integrity between `relations.tsv` and `relations/`), and the spec version pins that `70-spec-pin-repin-and-drift-gate` and `76-upstream-standards-pins` describe.

**A spec repo is not exempt from gating — it is the repo where an unnoticed defect propagates furthest**, because agora, cuneiform and every export vendor these schemas and this registry by drift-gated copy. A malformed `relations.tsv` merged here becomes a failing drift gate in four downstream repos.

Follow cuneiform's `196` shape: a CHANGED-PATH-SCOPED dispatch table, not a single blunt command — `.chief/verify.sh --plan` printing the selection without running, and `.chief/verify-test.sh` asserting the mapping.

userStories.title: Wire the checks that already exist
userStories.description: The cheapest possible first step: koine already ships two guards that nothing runs at merge.
acceptanceCriteria: `.chief/verify.sh` dispatches on the changed paths (`git diff --name-only $CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH...HEAD`) and runs `check-doc-integrity.mjs` for any `**/*.md` change and `check-tasklist-categories.mjs` for any `tasks/chief/**` change, exiting NON-ZERO on the first failure.
An unmatched path falls back to running everything, so a new file class is gated by default rather than silently ungated — cuneiform's `196` rule.
`.chief/verify.sh --plan` prints the selection without running anything, and a `.chief/verify-test.sh` asserts the path→gate mapping so the dispatch is checkable rather than read.

**Prove it BLOCKS**: a deliberately broken branch (a dangling Markdown link) is shown to fail the gate, and the proof is recorded in the notes. A gate nobody has seen refuse is not known to work — this is the story `196` credited with catching a real pre-existing defect.
userStories.notes: verify.sh is now a changed-path dispatch table (4 gates: guard-doc-integrity, guard-doc-links, guard-categories, verify-selftest); unruled paths select the umbrella = every gate. .chief/verify-test.sh: 21 passed, 0 failed. Real branch gate green (rc=0, doc-integrity OK on 35 files / 572 links, doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main). BLOCK PROOF: on a scratch branch a dangling link appended to README.md made the gate exit rc=1 — 'gate "guard-doc-integrity" FAILED (selected by changed path README.md) - blocking merge'; branch discarded, gate back to rc=0. Wiring it also caught a real pre-existing defect: docs/README.md:8 linked out of the repo to ../../rosetta/... — converted to a text citation.

userStories.title: Gate the assets a spec repo actually ships
userStories.description: Schemas and the shared registry are what downstream repos vendor. A defect here propagates by drift gate into agora, cuneiform and every export.
acceptanceCriteria: Every `schemas/*.schema.json` is validated as JSON Schema and every `$ref` is asserted to resolve — a schema that parses but whose refs dangle validates nothing downstream.

`registry/*.tsv` is gated for column shape, duplicate ids, and referential integrity between `relations.tsv` and `relations/` — the registry is the file ADR-0013's whole no-relation-coined rule depends on, and cuneiform's `render::fabric` vendors it byte-identically.
The guards live in `scripts/` beside the existing two and are runnable standalone, so CI and a developer run the same command — never a check that exists only inside the hook.
Each new guard is MUTATION-CHECKED and the mutation recorded: break a `$ref`, duplicate a registry id, and confirm each fails. An unmutated guard is a guess.
userStories.notes: Two new standalone guards beside the existing two: `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs` (9 schemas, 274 schema positions, 78 $refs, 3 fixtures — draft-2020-12 dialect, $id matches path, every key at a schema position is a real keyword, every $ref resolves file-then-pointer) and `node scripts/check-registry.mjs` (7 TSVs, 27 relation names unique across the core file and every domain file — column shape, duplicate ids, and the cross-file pointers: domain prefix vs `domain`, media-types `lineage_relation` -> a declared relation, entity-types `refinement_enum` -> an enum file whose token column matches). Both wired into .chief/verify.sh as guard-schemas / guard-registry with narrow rules (`schemas/*.schema.json`, `schemas/fixtures/*.json`, `registry/*.tsv`); `scripts/*` now selects all five guards. MUTATION-CHECKED, 8 mutations, all rc=1: M1 $ref nodeRef->nodeReff (dangles), M2 additionalProperties->additionalProperies (not a keyword), M3 $id drifted from filename, M4 duplicate relation id part_of, M5 a row missing a tab (7 fields, header declares 8), M6 lineage_relation media:transcoded_from names no relation, M7 an unregistered registry TSV, M8 soc:spouse_of stripped of its prefix; tree restored, both guards rc=0 after. verify-test.sh: 30 passed, 0 failed. Full branch gate CHIEF_BASE_BRANCH=main .chief/verify.sh: rc=0, all six gates green (doc-integrity OK 35 files/572 links, doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main, categories 20 tasklists, schemas OK, registry OK, selftest 30/30).
